transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Mon Jul 21 2025 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Nadia Ruiz (Redwood Partner AM), Ravi Patel (AtlasGrid Head of Platform), Sasha Ivanov (AtlasGrid Director of AI), Miguel Santos (AtlasGrid Infrastructure), Leah Ortiz (Procurement)
Recording: (fireflies auto)

Auto-summary (may be incomplete): Partner GTM alignment, account prioritization, pilot scope, procurement questions, next steps to share docs and run a perf sanity check.

Topics: account prioritization, co-sell routing, pilot scope, pricing/reseller split, security/compliance checklist, benchmark plan.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro - Maya Chen, AE on Redwood inference, Ethan our SE, and Nadia from partner go-to-market. 
[00:12] Ravi Patel: Hi, thanks — Ravi here. We're excited, been talking about this internally.
[00:17] Sasha Ivanov: Sasha — we'll be the product sponsor from AtlasGrid.
[00:21] Leah Ortiz: Leah in procurement — I'll be handling legal and contract questions.
[00:25] Maya Chen: Great. Quick agenda: prioritize accounts for co-sell, agree on lead routing and margin expectations, and define a minimal pilot. Does that work?
[00:32] Miguel Santos: yes sounds good.
[00:35] Ethan Park: I'll start with a very short technical framing so we can scope the pilot correctly, then we can jump into account lists.
[00:42] Ethan Park: At a high level Redwood can run hosted inference or dedicated pools, and we support private deployments into a VPC or on-prem with a private control plane. For pilot we usually recommend dedicated reserved capacity if you need predictable latency, but for early benching hosted or a small dedicated pool is fine.
[01:04] Sasha Ivanov: Real question for us — how long does a dedicated spin up take? We have some regulated customers who want private control plane.
[01:10] Maya Chen: Typical time varies: hosted is immediate, dedicated can be provisioned in days to a week depending on availability, private on-prem is longer and needs the infra work. For co-sell pilot we can do hosted with a private tenancy model or a small dedicated pod.
[01:22] Ravi Patel: On the enterprise side, our sales lead wants to see reseller economics — what's the margin split and how do referral credits work?
[01:29] Nadia Ruiz: Good question. We have a standard reseller grid; we can propose a deal desk credit for closed-won brought by AtlasGrid plus lead registration. I'll attach the grid. Typically referral credit is 10-20% depending on commitment.
[01:40] Leah Ortiz: We'll need the reseller agreement and any sample SOWs, and our legal team will want to redline. Also need to know about data residency — any EU controls?
[01:50] Maya Chen: We support region-specific hosting; for EU customers we can pin region and meet data residency controls. We'll share security and SOC2 docs.
[01:58] Ethan Park: Just to flag potential gotcha: when customers want private on-prem, we need to talk KMS and HSM integrations early — sometimes those are the blockers. Fireflies transcribed "Key-ems" earlier in another call, so apologies if that shows up in docs.
[02:12] Ravi Patel: haha, noted. For prioritization, we curated a list of accounts we think are highest potential — about 20. We want help narrowing to top 10 where co-sell will move the needle.
[02:22] Maya Chen: Perfect. Can you share the raw list and add a data point: current AI maturity + champion contact? That lets us score for fit and ease-of-sale.
[02:33] Ravi Patel: Yeah. We'll export from Salesforce. Side note — we use SFDC and would like lead registration to sync into our instance; is that supported?
[02:41] Nadia Ruiz: We do partner lead registration via our partner portal and have API hooks to push leads into SFDC. We'll coordinate mapping.
[02:48] Sasha Ivanov: On the technical split for the pilot — we want to validate latency and cost per 1k tokens at varying sequence lengths. Can you do a quick bench?
[02:56] Ethan Park: Totally. For a quick sanity bench we can run 5-10 prompts across model variants (quantized small, base float) and 3 sequence lengths. We can run on Redwood hosted in their region or on a small dedicated instance if you prefer. It should take a day to run once we have access.
[03:12] Miguel Santos: We'll provide a sandbox network and IAM user. How do we share credentials?
[03:18] Maya Chen: We'll use a short-lived service account and secure transfer; we'll send our security checklist.
[03:23] Leah Ortiz: Procurement will also want pricing for committed reserved capacity vs Pay-as-you-go.
[03:29] Maya Chen: We'll include pricing scenarios. For dedicated the break-even is usually visible in the account plan; we'll model that in the joint account plan template.
[03:37] Ravi Patel: On GTM — what marketing assets will you co-brand? We want an email, one-pager, and possibly a joint webinar.
[03:45] Nadia Ruiz: We can co-brand a one-pager and co-host a webinar. Let's pick the top 3 accounts for targeted outreach first.
[03:52] Sasha Ivanov: Also, can Redwood provide reference architecture diagrams for the private deployment flow? Our infra team will want to see the network hops and audit log locations.
[04:01] Ethan Park: Yes — we'll share an architecture doc. Quick caveat: sometimes Fireflies or transcript tools mess up Kubernetes or KV-cache names, so I'll make sure the doc uses the exact internal names so there's no confusion.
[04:14] Maya Chen: Let's move to account prioritization — Ravi, can you walk us through how you scored the 20?
[04:20] Ravi Patel: Sure. We ranked by ARR, AI maturity, procurement velocity, existing infra using GPUs, and whether they have an internal ML platform team. Early on we thought of a two-tier approach: tier A top 10 for immediate co-sell outreach, tier B for nurture.
[04:35] Maya Chen: OK. Redwood suggestion: prioritize accounts where latency/cost sensitivity is high for the customer (we can show typical unit economics), and where there's an internal champion who already pushed an initial POC. That lets us close faster.
[04:48] Miguel Santos: One of the accounts in our top 10 uses a lot of edge inference and has intermittent connectivity — they'd require on-prem clusters or a hybrid model. How does Redwood support hybrid?
[04:58] Ethan Park: Hybrid is doable; we can split inference between local edge nodes and Redwood private core for heavy workloads. But that increases integration complexity and we should scope as a separate workstream.
[05:12] Sasha Ivanov: Are there any competitors already in these accounts?
[05:16] Ravi Patel: some have pilots with Anthropic and one with Vertex. We can try to displace if the business case is strong.
[05:23] Maya Chen: Good to know. On displacement we often highlight cost/latency and the unified operations across dedicated and private. We'll prepare a short competitive battlecard tailored to each target.
[05:33] Leah Ortiz: Legal question — do you have a standard reseller contract? We need to compare terms to our master supplier agreement.
[05:39] Nadia Ruiz: Yes — we'll send the reseller agreement and a sample SOW. Expect the partner-specific terms and referral mechanics.
[05:46] Ravi Patel: For the pilot SOW can we keep it small — maybe 8 weeks, success criteria: latency under X ms for 95th percentile and 20% lower cost than current baseline.
[05:58] Ethan Park: We'll help define the metrics precisely. Note that sequence length distribution matters a lot; if your customers use long context (2–4k tokens) the unit cost differs a lot.
[06:10] Sasha Ivanov: Most of the target accounts have mid-length contexts (~1k tokens) but some generative use cases push longer sequences.
[06:17] Maya Chen: OK. For the immediate co-sell outreach, propose we each assign a sales lead to the top 10: AtlasGrid maps the champion and initial contact, Redwood will provide a sequence of collateral + a champion intro.
[06:29] Ravi Patel: We'll do that. We'll also expect a simple lead scoring rubric to prioritize outreach.
[06:34] Maya Chen: We'll send a scoring template.
[06:36] Miguel Santos: Technical: what about RBAC and SSO? We need to ensure AtlasGrid can map roles to their sales users.
[06:44] Ethan Park: We support SAML SSO and can map roles; RBAC is configurable. For private deployments, we integrate with customer KMS; for hosted we expose per-tenant encryption with our keys or customer-managed keys.
[06:58] Leah Ortiz: Will need a security addendum for KMS/HSM usage.
[07:03] Maya Chen: We'll include the security addendum and SOC2 docs in the packet we send.
[07:08] Sasha Ivanov: For timeline, we want to run the first pilot outreach by mid-August. Is that realistic?
[07:15] Maya Chen: Yes, if we get the account list and champions this week or next and run the bench quickly. That aligns with an outreach start mid-August.
[07:24] Nadia Ruiz: I'll propose 3 time slots for an exec intro next week and loop in your sales leadership.
[07:30] Ravi Patel: Great. Any other blockers from AtlasGrid side?
[07:33] Leah Ortiz: From procurement, we just need reseller pricing, contract and proof of SOC2 and KMS approach.
[07:39] Maya Chen: We'll package that.
[07:41] Ethan Park: Quick technical note — for the bench please provide a small prompt set and expected token distribution. We prefer representative prompts; don't send sensitive PII in the test set.
[07:52] Miguel Santos: noted. We'll scrub PII.
[07:55] Maya Chen: Alright let's recap: Redwood to send joint account plan template, pricing scenarios, reseller agreement, SOC2/security docs, and a proposed bench plan. AtlasGrid to send top 12 (we said 12 earlier) accounts with champions and a sandbox for the bench. Schedule exec intro and set pilot SOW expectations.
[08:12] Ravi Patel: Sounds good.
[08:15] Sasha Ivanov: Quick micro-question: for referrals, if AtlasGrid sources a deal but Redwood runs the pilot, who captures the credit?
[08:23] Nadia Ruiz: We'll register the lead in partner portal and tag the AE — deal desk will adjudicate credit based on lead registration and proof of handoff. We usually honor early registration plus engagement milestones.
[08:34] Leah Ortiz: One more legal nuance: we may need indemnities mapped to our supply contracts. We'll flag specifics after review.
[08:40] Maya Chen: Thanks Leah. We'll be responsive to redlines.
[08:44] Ethan Park: I'll follow up on the bench steps and prerequisites in an email with a short checklist.
[08:50] Maya Chen: Great. Any final questions?
[08:52] Ravi Patel: No, thanks everyone.
[08:54] Maya Chen: Appreciate the time. We'll send the packet today/tomorrow and get moving.
[08:58] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription quality: medium — a few acronyms mangled by auto-transcription (KMS/HSM, RBAC spelled out oddly, and some product names).

Referenced artifacts: "joint-account-plan-template.xlsx" (will be shared), "reseller-grid.pdf", security packet link placeholder, bench prompt set (to be provided by AtlasGrid).

Recap/Next steps (short): share docs, AtlasGrid shares account list + sandbox, schedule exec intro, Redwood runs quick bench and prepares pilot SOW.
